newsitem.title: USA: Iraqi opposition unaware of Saddam offensive.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi opposition unaware of Saddam offensive.

text.p: An Iraqi close to opposition leaders said late on Thursday he had heard nothing of a new large-scale offensive by President Saddam Hussein against Shi'ite villages in the south.
Salem Chalabi, an attorney, and nephew of Ahmad Chalabi, the head of the London-based Iraqi National Congress, said he last spoke to his contacts early on Thursday.

He was commenting on news reports that an Iraqi opposition leader in Cairo said that about 3,000 Iraqi troops backed by artillery and tanks were involved in an assault on rebels in the marshes of Al-Mugtaa and Al-Hayader near Basra on Tuesday.
Chalabi said Saddam Hussein had been attacking the Shi'ites for a long period, at times using tanks and other types of heavy weapons he should not be deploying.

"It has been going on for about two years in the marshes. What has been happening in the last year is that there has been a lot of infiltration from armed groups and there has been warfare at night," he added.
Iraqi army convoys have been hit and in response soldiers have been firing on villages they say are haboring rebels.
"I would be surprised of a large-scale offensive because there aren't any large scale concentrations of opposition groups or rebels," he said.

On Tuesday, Iraq said three mortar bombs were fired at the Baghdad headquarters of an Iranian opposition group, killing one person and injuring several others. Iraq laid blame for the attack on Tehran.
The bombs landed a few metres from the headquarters of the Mujahideen Khalq group, which has military bases close to the border with Iran and has vowed to topple Tehran's government.
